τῇ αἰσχρότητι τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν συναποθνήσκοντες, σὺν τῷ πονηρῷ αὐτῶν ἐφευρετῇ
πονηρῶς τακήσονται· ὑπὸ δὲ τῶν παριόντων τὴν κακίαν, γνωρίζεται τῆς
ἀναμαρτησίας ἡ παιδεία τοῦ ἀκάκου. Ἡσυχία ἐστὶν ἀποχὴ κακίας ἐμπράκτου καὶ ὁρά
σεων, ἣν οἱ ἀγαθοὶ ἡσυχάζουσιν· οἱ δὲ τοῦ νοὸς καὶ σώματος ὀφθαλμοὶ τῶν κακῶν,
πάντα τὸν χρόνον ἐπι νοοῦνται κακά. Ὁ δὲ συνετὸς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ᾅδου τοῦ τῶν
ἁμαρτω λῶν· ὁδοὶ ζωῆς, διανοήματα θείων λόγων καὶ ἔργων· ὁ δὲ συνετὸς ἀεὶ ταῦτα
ποιεῖ καὶ διδάσκει, ἵνα σὺν τοῖς μαθητιῶσιν ἐκκλίνας ἐκ τοῦ ᾅδου σωθῇ. Οἱ τὰς
ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ μὴ πράττοντες, ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ εἰσιν· φίλοι δὲ αὐτοῦ γίνονται ἐπὰν τοῖς
δικαίοις προσδράμωσιν, ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς πράξεις αὑτῶν τὰς πονηράς· ἐξ ὧν
ἐναχθέντες ὡς ἐκεῖνοι τὰς ζωοποιοὺς ὁδοὺς πορεύσονται· Παύλου κηρύξαντος, Οἵ
ποτε ὄντες ἐχθροὶ, κατηλλάγησαν τῷ Θεῷ διὰ τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ·
προσεκτέον ὅτι πάντες οἱ ἐχθροὶ, διὰ τῶν δικαίων φίλοι γίνο
pass_a_gloss:
Sinners perish in disgrace, sharing the fate of their own evil inventions. Yet, by observing those who overcome wickedness, the blameless training of the innocent is revealed. Quiet means refraining from harmful actions and evil sights—what the virtuous maintain in calm. Meanwhile, the wicked, with mind and body fixed on evil, constantly dwell on it. The sensible avoid the realm of the dead where sinners dwell; instead, they walk life’s paths, meditating on God’s words and actions, teaching these so they and their students may flee Hades and live. Disobeying his orders makes one his enemy; but turning to the just and admitting evil conduct turns enemies into friends—moved by this, they walk life-giving roads, as Paul declared: former enemies reconciled to God by Christ’s death. Remember: all enemies gain friendship through the just, so Christ may say: I no longer call you servants, but friends. Again, wisdom is needed there to effect reconciliation—either the one versed in penalty-speech is an angel, or God’s wrath is voiced. The wise, aligned with God in deed and word, remain unafraid. Wisdom’s nests are churches or heavenly tabernacles; wisdom itself is Christ, God’s Son. Understanding’s nests surpass silver: they are active virtues—righteousness, insight, prudence, fortitude, endurance. Gentleness without rebuke, no anger, mercy, faith with hope and love—by these, like ladder steps, one enters wisdom’s dwelling freely, those who wish to go up and remain.

Discipline is fear of God, fasting, self-control, watchfulness, singing, and the training that comes in sickness as God’s test.

Rebukes are God’s commandments, for they convict us when we sin.

The ways are the senses; guarding them keeps the soul from death toward life, for life gives life to all, brings being from nothing—the Holy Trinity; loving life, striving always to live in it, one avoids mouthing non-divine words and deeds, and draws near to God’s knowledge.

God is life; the source of His self-existent triple wisdom is wisdom, knowledge, virtues; from this spring, drinkers share immortality and endless life; those who hold this spring have understanding of life’s words; but the foolish’s discipline is folly, and uncontrolled discipline is foolishness.

Knowledge is recognition, for it knows all things; the wise heart perceives what comes from its own mouth, in bodily and incorporeal judgment, and what they do, they teach and do.

Demons, learning words from the devil, act against the holy, imagining they can split them from knowledge. She by nature binds them to friendship with heavenly powers. Solomon, I think, shows this in the proverb: calling Satan a twisted man; those going about with lamps of deceit—false teachers on his side—he calls evil demons; but friends are the holy ones who through knowledge touch God and each other. The devil is a lawless man; he tries to tempt God’s friends and leads them to destructive, not good, ways; when he deceives a holy one, he fixes thoughts in his own eyes, counts them twisted, lest he save the repentance of whom he hunted; he nibbles with his lips on his eyes all evil thoughts, renunciation and all pleasure of licentiousness; he is a furnace of all wickedness, kindling in it the souls of those about to be destroyed; but the divine Spirit quenches this furnace’s flame, shaking wisdom like dew; yet many still wicked men in it imitate their father, the devil. He said here bosoms are hearts of the unjust; I think everywhere bosom means either mind or knowledge; the wicked the devil embraces in his bosom, but the righteous the Lord. If every sin-doer is a slave, and every one departing from wickedness through virtue held as masters foolish demons—who also is God’s house of mysteries—
pass_b_english:
They die in the shame of their sins, and along with the evil they have invented, they will be dealt with wickedly. However, through those who pass by wickedness, the education of the innocent is recognized as blameless. Quietness is the abstinence from active evil and from seeing evils, which the good practice in stillness. But the eyes of the mind and body of the wicked are constantly contemplating evil throughout all time. Yet the prudent person is not in Hades with the sinners; rather, the ways of life, the thoughts of divine words and deeds—these the prudent person always does and teaches, so that, turning away with their disciples from Hades, they may be saved. Those who do not practice his commandments are his enemies; but they become his friends when they run to the righteous, confessing their wicked deeds. Having been moved by these things, just as those others, they will go on the life-giving ways. For Paul proclaimed: Those who once were enemies were reconciled to God through the death of his Son. Take heed that all enemies, through the righteous, become friends—so that Christ may say to all: No longer do I call you slaves, but friends. Again, there, wisdom is needed to make atonement; either the one who knows the words about punishment is an angel, or the wrath of God is spoken. The wise person in divine works and words, being of one mind with him, will not be startled by him. Nests of wisdom are the churches, or the tents in the heaven; but wisdom is Jesus Christ, the Son of God. Moreover, nests of understanding are better than silver, namely, the practical virtues: justice, knowledge, wisdom, self-control, courage, patience.

Unrebukeable gentleness, freedom from anger, mercy, and faith joined with hope and love: through these, as if climbing the rungs of a ladder, one may enter without hindrance into the dwellings of wisdom, those who wish to ascend and dwell there.

He speaks of discipline as the fear of God, fasting, self-control, vigilance, hymnody, and the discipline that comes upon us in sickness as a testing from God.

He calls rebukes the commandments of God, for these indeed rebuke us when we sin.

He says the ways here are the senses; and the one who guards them preserves his own soul from death toward life, for life is that which sustains all living things, and brings into being from non-existence the Holy Trinity, which causes to be. And the one who loves life, and ever strives to live in it, will refrain from his own mouth the words and works not of God, and will draw near to the knowledge of God.

God is life; and the source of His self-existent, triple-wisdom life is wisdom, knowledge, and the virtues; from this spring those who drink partake of immortality and eternal life; but for those who possess such a spring, there is an understanding of the words of life; yet the discipline of the foolish is folly, and the undisciplined discipline is folly.

He said that knowledge is recognition, because it recognizes all things; and the heart of the wise perceives what comes from its own mouth, both in bodily judgment and in incorporeal matters, and whatever they themselves do, they teach and practice.

The demons, learning words from the devil, attempt against the holy, and imagine themselves trying to separate them from knowledge.

This is her nature, by which she binds them in friendship with the heavenly powers; and the same thing, I believe, Solomon has indicated by this proverb, saying that the twisted man is Satan; but those going about bearing lamps of deceit—namely, the false teachers on his side—he calls evil demons; yet friends, namely, the holy ones, those who through knowledge are touching God and one another. A lawless man, the devil is; and he attempts to tempt the friends of God, and he leads them away to the ways of destruction and not of goodness; but when he has deceived any one of the holy ones, he establishes thoughts for his own eyes, and he considers them twisted, lest perhaps he should save the repentance of him whom he has hunted; and he nibbles with his lips upon his eyes all the evil thoughts, both renunciation and all pleasure of licentiousness; this one is a furnace of all wickedness, and he kindles within it the souls of those who are about to be destroyed; but of this furnace, the divine Spirit quenches the flame, shaking forth wisdom like dew; yet many still of those who are in it, wicked men, are accustomed to imitate their father, the devil. He has said here that the bosoms are the hearts of the unjust; but I think also that everywhere the bosom signifies either the mind, or knowledge; and the wicked indeed the devil embraces in his bosom, but the righteous the Lord. If every one who practices sin is a slave, and every one who departs from wickedness through virtue has held as masters the foolish demons—who also is the house of mysteries of God—
